title: Exclusion Constraints (EXCLUDE)
description: Prevent scheduling overlaps and spatial collisions at the database layer using GiST-backed exclusion constraints.

data.text: A **UNIQUE constraint** only checks for equality (`=`). But what if you need to guarantee that no two hotel bookings overlap in time (`&&`) or no two meeting room reservations collide? PostgreSQL's **`EXCLUDE` constraint** generalizes uniqueness across arbitrary operators using GiST indexes.

data.title: Preventing Room Booking Conflicts with EXCLUDE USING gist
data.content: Ensures no single room can have overlapping booking periods.

data.title: Eliminates Application-Level Race Conditions
data.text: Without exclusion constraints, preventing scheduling double-bookings requires complex distributed locks or serialized transactions. Exclusion constraints guarantee 100% collision prevention directly inside PostgreSQL.
How an Exclusion Constraint Differs From Unique

`UNIQUE` is the special case of `EXCLUDE` where the operator is `=`. `EXCLUDE` lets you supply **any** indexed operator, and requires that at least one pair be non-`=` — otherwise you would just write a unique index. It is backed by a GiST or SP-GiST index, so equality on a scalar column needs the `btree_gist` extension to be indexable by GiST.

data.text: Deferrable: Let the Transaction Resolve Itself

An exclusion constraint can be `DEFERRABLE`, which is essential when you move a booking by a minute in a single transaction: deleting and re-inserting would otherwise trip the constraint mid-transaction.

data.title: A Partial Exclusion Constraint
data.code:
CREATE TABLE product_promotions (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    period     DATERANGE NOT NULL,
    closed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    EXCLUDE USING gist (product_id WITH =, period WITH &&)
        WHERE (NOT closed)
);

data.title: Interview Answer
data.text: The phrase to remember is **"uniqueness over an operator, not just equality"**. A booking system enforces non-overlap with `EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, stay WITH &&)`, and because the check runs inside the database it is safe under concurrent inserts with no application locking.

Would a partial index (`WHERE ...`) express the rule more precisely?

items.question: What is the difference between `EXCLUDE` and `UNIQUE`?
items.answer: `UNIQUE` enforces `=` across the listed columns. `EXCLUDE` lets you name the operator for each column, so you can enforce `&&` (overlap) or geometric relations. A `EXCLUDE` with only `=` operators requires the `btree_gist` extension for scalar columns but is otherwise equivalent to `UNIQUE`.

items.question: Why does `EXCLUDE` need `btree_gist`?
items.answer: GiST indexes do not natively support btree operators such as `=` for scalar types. `btree_gist` adds that support so a scalar column can participate in a GiST exclusion constraint.

items.question: What happens on a conflict?
items.answer: The statement fails with `conflicting key value violates exclusion constraint`, and the `DETAIL` names the existing row. Because it is a normal constraint, the whole statement rolls back.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `EXCLUDE` enforces non-overlapping conditions across arbitrary operators.
Requires a GiST index and often the `btree_gist` extension.
The definitive database-level solution for calendar scheduling and booking systems.
